name: vwap_gap_fill_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Stocks that gap open >0.5% away from previous day's closing VWAP (not just previous close, but previous session's final VWAP value) tend to fill that gap within the first 90 minutes. Previous day VWAP represents the volume-weighted institutional consensus from the prior session. An overnight gap away from it is often driven by pre-market news overreaction, global cues, or Nifty futures movement that may not fully apply to individual stocks. The inefficiency exists because gap fills are well-known for gaps from previous close but not from previous VWAP — using VWAP as the anchor provides a better mean to revert to because it accounts for where most volume actually transacted, not just the arbitrary last-traded price.
mechanism: VWAP is the institutional execution benchmark. When spot deviates significantly from session VWAP, algorithmic execution engines increase order flow to mean-revert their fills toward VWAP. This creates measurable gravitational pull, especially during lower-volume mid-session periods when fewer competing flows are present.

conditions: close > low of first 5 bars (gap not extending)
close < high of first 5 bars (gap not extending)

exit.signal_exit: exit if gap extends beyond 2x original gap size (strong directional move)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 20; gap fills are less reliable in high-vol regimes
filters.volume_filter: opening volume > 1.5x average first-bar volume (confirms gap is being traded)

weaknesses: Gaps caused by genuine fundamental news (earnings, upgrades) may never fill — the event filter is imperfect
Opening 15 minutes have wide spreads and high slippage; actual slippage may be 5-8 bps not 3 bps
On days with strong global cues (US market crash/rally), most stocks gap together and fill rates drop sharply
prior_art: Gap fill strategies are extensively documented (Pristine.com, Gap-and-Go by Ross Cameron). Using previous VWAP as the anchor instead of previous close is less common. Bulkowski ('Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns') notes ~70% of gaps fill within the session but this includes multi-day holds. Intraday-only gap fill has lower fill rates.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
